plan: With 3 bidders and uniform value distribution on [0,49], the standard first-price auction Nash equilibrium strategy is to bid (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for 3 bidders. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $31, so optimal bid ≈ $20.67. This shades my bid appropriately below value to maximize expected profit while maintaining competitive winning chances against Betty and Charles.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $37, so optimal bid ≈ $37 × 2/3 = $24.7. This maximizes expected profit by not overpaying while still having a reasonable chance to win against the other two bidders.

With 3 bidders and independent private values uniform on $0-$49, the optimal first-price auction bidding strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, i.e., 2/3 of my value, to maximize expected profit. My value is $11, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 * 11 = $7.3. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin if I win.
